chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Playing the O'Ryan club in Atlantic City
summary: The band played a new club with four saxophones, working nine to five with a breakfast show; McRae practiced bass in the empty club.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And we had this beautiful band. First time they had four saxophones in there. We went in there with four saxophones.
Who were the other two saxophone players?
Oh boy. It's been so long. See, the only thing about that band -- see, it's very hard to remember who those fellows were, because you understand, we only had this band together for one summer.
The whole time I was there, I -- we used to work in a night club and it'll be all night long. And we get off like five or six o'clock in the morning.
I'd just stay 'round the club and practice a little bit.
You started around nine at night?
So it was a nine to five gig --

Yeah, it was a long gig. Because we always had a breakfast dance. You know, a breakfast show. Something like Sunday mornings we get off at six o'clock in the morning -- seven o'clock because you had that breakfast show start at five. I'd stay in the club and practice on my bass. Everybody will be gone and I'd stay in the club and practice, practice, practice, you know. Then I'd go home and get some sleep, like that.
You also had a little training on piano that your older brother helped you with, or did you --
